scope: Clinical nutrition rules for Indian students, hostel/PG residents and young adults. Educational guidance, not a medical diagnosis.

synergies.rule: Vitamin C + Iron = up to 3x absorption. Vitamin C converts ferric iron to the more absorbable ferrous form.
synergies.how: Squeeze half a lemon on dal, rajma, chana or palak; eat a guava or amla with poha or sprouts.

synergies.rule: A pinch of black pepper raises curcumin absorption roughly 20x (piperine slows its breakdown).
synergies.how: Add a pinch of kali mirch to haldi doodh or any haldi-based sabzi; fat (ghee/milk) helps further.

synergies.rule: Fat-soluble vitamins need fat to be absorbed. A low-fat meal can cut beta-carotene and Vitamin D uptake sharply.
synergies.how: Take Vitamin D with the main meal; cook carrots/greens with 1 tsp ghee or oil.

synergies.rule: Cereals are low in lysine, pulses are low in methionine; together they form a complete protein.
synergies.how: Dal-chawal, rajma-chawal, khichdi, idli-sambar — aim for roughly 1 part dal to 2-3 parts cereal.

synergies.rule: Fermenting (idli/dosa batter, curd, kanji) reduces phytates and raises B-vitamin and mineral availability.
synergies.how: Prefer fermented breakfasts; overnight-soaked or sprouted moong also cuts phytates.

synergies.rule: Vitamin D is required for intestinal calcium absorption; low D makes dairy calcium far less useful.
synergies.how: 15-20 minutes of midday sun on arms; pair with curd, paneer, ragi.

blockers.rule: Tannins in Chai block Iron — tea with a meal can cut non-heme iron absorption by 60% or more.
blockers.fix: Keep chai/coffee at least 45-60 minutes away from iron-rich meals; never drink chai with poha, dal or palak.

blockers.rule: Calcium competes with iron for absorption when eaten in the same meal.
blockers.fix: Separate iron tablets or iron-rich meals from milk/calcium supplements by about 2 hours.

blockers.blocker: Phytates in unsoaked whole grains, bran and legumes
blockers.rule: Phytic acid binds minerals and lowers their absorption.
blockers.fix: Soak dals and rajma 6-8 hours, sprout moong/chana, or ferment batters.

blockers.blocks: Calcium and iron from the same leaf
blockers.rule: Palak's oxalates bind most of its own calcium and iron, so palak alone is a weak iron source.
blockers.fix: Blanch palak and add lemon; rely on rajma, chana, til, jaggery-with-lemon, or eggs/meat for iron too.

blockers.rule: Long-term acid suppression and metformin lower B12 absorption.
blockers.fix: Ask the doctor about a B12 test if on these for more than a few months; vegetarians are at extra risk.

blockers.rule: High caffeine raises urinary calcium loss and disrupts sleep, which worsens appetite control.
blockers.fix: Cap at 2-3 cups a day and none after 4 PM.

hostel_constraints.rule: Assume only an electric kettle and hot water. Never suggest frying, pressure-cooking, baking or a stove.
options: Soya chunks soaked 10 min in kettle-hot water, squeezed, with lemon and chaat masala (~26 g protein per 50 g, about Rs 12)
Eggs boiled in the kettle for 12 minutes (about 6 g protein each)
Instant oats or poha softened with hot water, topped with peanuts
Sattu shake: 40 g sattu + water + lemon + salt (~8 g protein, about Rs 8)
Sprouted moong chaat with tomato, onion and lemon (no cooking needed)

hostel_constraints.rule: Prefer shelf-stable foods: roasted chana, peanuts, makhana, sattu, oats, bananas, guava, peanut chikki. Buy curd daily in small packs.
Optimise within the mess: take extra dal or curd, fill half the plate with sabzi, limit the second helping of rice, ask for lemon.

hostel_constraints.constraint: Student budget (about Rs 2000-4000 per month extra food spend)
hostel_constraints.rule: Cheapest protein per rupee: soya chunks, eggs, sattu, chana, peanuts, curd. Avoid whey and imported foods unless the budget allows.

condition_rules.rule: Low-GI swaps: millets or brown rice for white rice, besan/bajra roti for maida, whole fruit not juice; protein at every meal; 10-15 min walk after meals.
Insulin-friendly plate: protein + fibre first, carbs last; include seeds (flax, pumpkin); limit sugary drinks.
Keep salt under 5 g/day; avoid pickles, papad and namkeen; add potassium from banana, coconut water, dal.

Days 1-3: ORS, coconut water, kanji, dal water. Days 4-7: moong dal khichdi, curd rice. Days 8-14: dal-roti, paneer/eggs to rebuild. See a doctor if fever lasts more than 3 days or any bleeding appears.
First 6-24 h: ORS sips and rest; then banana, rice kanji, curd rice, toast; avoid dairy-heavy, fried and spicy food for 3-5 days.

safety: NutriPath AI is not a doctor: do not diagnose or prescribe medicine doses.
Red flags (chest pain, fainting, bleeding, fever above 3 days, severe dehydration, dengue warning signs) require immediate medical care.
Always respect the user's stated allergies and diet type.
Recommend blood tests (CBC, ferritin, B12, Vitamin D) before suggesting high-dose supplements.
